author: Nayan Seth
description:
The Trump administration on Wednesday said that China is on track to meet its agricultural purchase commitments, with the sector expected to feature prominently in the deliverables for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping’s talks in Washington later this month.
“China is ramping up their purchases,” said Luke Lindberg, the US Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs at the US Department of Agriculture (USDA). “We’re seeing that progress happen.”
Speaking...
title: US says China ‘on track’ to fulfil farm purchases ahead of Xi’s Washington visit

author: Nayan Seth,Dewey Sim,Khushboo Razdan
description:
China is willing to help broker a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, sources have said just weeks before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected in Washington for a bilateral summit.
Multiple people familiar with the matter told the South China Morning Post that Beijing was stepping up to play an “active” and “constructive” role in reviving US-North Korea diplomacy, underscoring its resolve to remain a central player in negotiations on the...
title: Once sidelined, China stands ready to broker a fourth Trump-Kim handshake

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
The Trump administration sanctioned Chinese-language marketplace Xinbi Guarantee on Wednesday, along with two affiliated organisations, as part of a wider crackdown on transnational cybercrime.
The US Department of Justice also announced it had seized Telegram channels and cryptocurrency wallets tied to the platform, which has over 650,000 users, freezing more than US$52 million in potentially laundered funds in just one day.
“This is not a distant overseas crime story,” said Jeanine Pirro, the...
title: US sanctions Chinese-language Xinbi Guarantee marketplace over cyber scams

author: Han Li
description:
Greg Reverdiau, an Arizona-based drone trainer, said he saw something highly unusual for politically polarised America when he waded through public comments on a US government proposal to restrict foreign-made drones: a consensus.
Reverdiau, the founder of Pilot Institute, which helps aviators obtain licences, said he reviewed over 3,800 comments submitted to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and estimates that about 98 per cent opposed the proposal or raised concerns about it.
“Those...
title: US drone ban proposal to combat China’s dominance concerns American police, farmers

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazil on Wednesday eliminated its federal import tax on small overseas parcels, moving in the opposite direction from US and European Union efforts to close a loophole that saw such Chinese retail giants as Shein and Temu expand rapidly.
The elimination will hurt the country’s tax base, but the levy on lower value shirts, electronics, toys and kitchen gadgets ultimately proved too unpopular among Brazilians ahead of the October 4 presidential election, forcing Brasilia to back down.
In an...
title: Brazil scraps tax on small parcels as Chinese platforms lose US and EU access

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The risk of a conflict over Taiwan is shaping Japanese defence planning, with Tokyo shoring up security at home and abroad for a potentially prolonged fight. But there are economic, demographic and political constraints on how far its military transformation can go. In the third of a three-part series, Gabriel Dominguez examines the various challenges confronting Japan in its bid to expand its military.
Driven by the growing risk that a conflict over Taiwan could draw Tokyo into a high-intensity...
title: Japan’s China-facing military build-up confronts labour, budget and political limits

author: Ling Xin
description:
A year after China unveiled the world’s first operational air-breathing hypersonic missiles, the United States is launching a programme to double down on developing similar weapons.
The US Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (Darpa) will bring contractors together later this month to lay out what it wants from the Next Generation Hypersonic Cruise Missile, with air-breathing propulsion at the heart of the project, according to the agency’s website.
Unlike rocket-powered missiles,...
title: US scrambles to match China’s air-breathing hypersonic missiles with Darpa programme

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Beijing has reinforced its military firepower facing the Taiwan Strait by deploying more 155mm PLZ-05 self-propelled howitzers, according to state media reports.
Replacing its older 122mm artillery, a heavy combined-arms brigade under the People’s Liberation Army’s 71st Group Army has been equipped with a batch of the 155mm self-propelled howitzers over the past two months and conducted its first live-fire test of the weapons, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Sunday.
The 71st Group Army...
title: Beijing boosts Taiwan-facing firepower with brigade-level 155mm howitzer deployment

author: Laura Zhou
description:
China has accused Philippine officials of “grandstanding and lying” after Manila’s defence secretary publicly read aloud a Chinese diplomat’s note on the South China Sea that the Philippine minister described as “coercion, bullying and aggression”.
“We urge certain people in the Philippines to stop this grandstanding and lying, and to protect China-Philippine relations and the peace and stability in the South China Sea,” Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said.

Mao was responding to...
title: Beijing tells Manila to ‘stop lying’ after minister exposes South China Sea note

author: Albee Zhang
description:
If mastering drone-swarm technology were not difficult enough, China is now tackling the more complex task of integrating uncrewed land, sea and air platforms, according to the country’s leading developer in the field.
In an article posted on China Electronics Technology Group Corporation’s (CETC) social media account on Sunday, the company’s Intelligent Technology Research Institute said drone-swarm technology was not merely “many drones flying together”, but an intelligent, distributed combat...
title: Merging air, land and sea swarms – the next frontier in China’s drone technology

author: Julie Zhang
description:
Biomedicine is set to feature in Hong Kong’s first five-year plan, due to be unveiled next week, as the city’s top officials signal closer medical cooperation across the Greater Bay Area.
Lending weight to those ambitions, global pharmaceutical company GSK emphasised its interest in expanding its role in the region’s biotech development on Wednesday, at the fifth Hong Kong International Biotechnology Conference and Exhibition (BIOHK).
Speaking at the event, Hong Kong Secretary for Health Lo...
title: Hong Kong targets biomedicine powerhouse status in debut 5-year plan

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Geologists say they have identified a new deposit in central China that can produce high-purity quartz comparable to the quality produced at a critical world-leading mine in the United States.
The high-purity quartz from the Chinese deposit is described as having “highly similar” properties to the resources produced at North Carolina’s Spruce Pine, which is crucial to the global production of solar panels and semiconductors.
In the US, there is a growing call from the industry to use high-purity...
title: Quartz deposit purity in central China ‘highly similar’ to US Spruce Pine standard: study

author: Fan Hou
title: US-China trade, tariffs in 2026

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. China’s radar satellites capture sharp images of glacier collapse site in Nepal
Within hours of a devastating glacier collapse on the China-Nepal border, a Beijing-based satellite company had already redirected six of its satellites to survey the disaster zone.
2. Chip expert Chen Ye joins China’s Zhejiang...
title: China-Nepal floods; arthritis drug restores alopecia patients’ hair: 7 science highlights

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Urgent priorities for advancing China’s philanthropy sector include fostering a favourable legal environment and overhauling the nation’s social service industry, according to leading policy experts at a forum in Hong Kong on Tuesday.
Mainland charitable organisations could learn from Hong Kong’s experience to increase their professional expertise, while the Greater Bay Area city cluster plan could be leveraged as a catalyst to boost the sector, they said.
The panel discussion – part of the Hong...
title: GBA integration may help mainland China philanthropy sector learn from Hong Kong

author: Julie Zhang
description:
Pharmaceutical companies have embraced artificial intelligence in drug research almost universally, yet few company executives expect AI to actually make drugs succeed, according to a Citi survey released on Tuesday.
“The biggest risk to the AI-powered drug discovery thesis is not that AI fails to accelerate discovery,” said John Yung, head of Asia healthcare research at the US investment bank. “The stronger risk is that acceleration does not translate into better drugs or higher probability of...
title: As China embraces AI, only 24% of US pharma execs bet on it for drug-making

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
The first two F-16 Block 70 fighters bought by Taipei from the United States have yet to reach Taiwan, after spending more than two weeks in Hawaii for reasons that remain unclear.
The aircraft, which were expected to arrive at Taiwan’s Chihhang Air Base in late August, were spotted preparing for departure at Joint Base Pearl Harbour-Hickam on Monday, raising expectations that the fighters were finally about to resume their journey.
But the two single-seat F-16Cs, numbered 6727 and 6728,...
title: Taiwan waits for its new F-16s, still stuck in Hawaii after a fortnight’s delay

author: Shi Huang
description:
Imagine swapping your daily cholesterol pill for a single injection that keeps “bad” cholesterol under control for a year, a decade – or even a lifetime.
Two clinical trials, one in the United States and another in China, suggest that this one-and-done approach could become a reality.
Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), better known as “bad” cholesterol, is a major driver of heart disease – the leading cause of death worldwide. Triglycerides, another type of blood fat, add to the...
title: US, China trials suggest a single nanodrug shot might stop bad cholesterol forever

author: Phoebe Zhang,Alcott Wei
description:
When you are denied a pay rise, when you feel anxious about your children’s education, or when you are alienated by colleagues, Chairman Mao can help.
At least, that is what China’s online influencers and their hundreds of thousands of followers believe.
Wednesday marks the 50th anniversary of the death of Mao Zedong, founding father of the People’s Republic of China. Chinese authorities have not announced any plans to mark the date, as former state leaders are usually commemorated on the...
title: Young Chinese turn to Mao Zedong for life advice, 50 years after his death

author: Alex Lo
description:
Argentine President Javier Milei has every right to reassert his country’s territorial claims over the Falkland Islands. His proposal to use the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration as a template for resolving the Falkland Islands dispute merits serious consideration as a pragmatic framework for bringing this long-standing territorial conflict to a peaceful conclusion.
Argentina’s claim to what its citizens call the Islas Malvinas rests on solid foundations. Upon independence from Spain in 1816,...
title: Britain should accept a Hong Kong-style handover of the Falklands
